# AzGuard

> Find and clean up forgotten and AI-agent-created cloud resources on Azure and AWS.

AzGuard is a free, open source command-line tool for Azure and AWS, published by Poietes LLC.

## CLI

Source checked: https://github.com/cdobratz/AzGuard commit bf3abbcc43020ec76defc048c4a43178750bb246 (main, 2026-11-18).

- `azguard cleanup` lists forgotten and AI-agent-created resources on Azure and AWS: idle disks, orphaned public IPs, NAT gateways, stopped-but-billed VMs, and the AWS equivalents. The default is a dry run. Pass `--apply` to delete. A resource tagged `azguard:keep=true` is never deleted.
- `azguard resources` lists the same resources and prints a monthly list-price estimate. The command is read-only.
- Free tier and credits come second. `azguard status`, `azguard scan`, `azguard budget`, and `azguard cost` cover Azure free-tier usage, budgets, and cost. `azguard aws` covers AWS free-tier usage and cost. `azguard init` records remaining Azure and AWS credits and when they expire. The limits files list 12 Azure services (`configs/free_tier_limits.yaml`) and 13 AWS services (`configs/aws_free_tier_limits.yaml`).
- `azguard watch` polls the Azure Activity Log and AWS CloudTrail. The default interval is 15 minutes. It can notify the desktop or a webhook you pass with `--webhook`.
- `azguard guard` checks billable commands against a session budget.
- The CLI has no telemetry client. It calls Azure and AWS for the command you run, public price-list APIs when an estimate needs them, and a webhook only when you set one.

`https://azguard.dev/install.sh` installs the latest GitHub release (v1.2.0 as of 2026-11-23) for linux and darwin, amd64 and arm64, after a sha256 check against that release's checksums.txt.
